answer: I would anchor trust in Proof of unique smoke alarm test record. With monthly tests logged at one address for years, a single jade check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so monthly tests logged at one address for years stays private; the lagoon is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the nadir of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
